what_happened: The predecessor oriented-forest work left an unusually complete landing pad: IsOrientedForest, saturation_of_orientedForest/' (hgen-parameterised), isOrientedForest_swap and ofStepRel_gen are all present in FormalSystem/Semantics/OrientedForest.lean, and TwoWayBounded + plus_invariance_of_isZTime are compiled in HistoryMorphism.lean with translationProduct_twoWayBounded as a two-line worked instance. Research needed no API discovery for the consumer side.

FrameOver.ofStep (FormalSystem/Semantics/IntNormalForm.lean:456) carries a [Finite W] binder solely to discharge saturation via TaskFrame.saturation_of_finite. The universal cover carrier is infinite by construction, so no existing constructor can build the cover frame; a Saturation-parameterised sibling constructor has to be added before the cover can be presented as a FrameOver intOrder.

SuccOrder (coe intOrder) does not synthesise (recorded at FormalSystem/Semantics/ShiftSet.lean:485): instance search runs at reducible transparency and intOrder.carrier is not syntactically Int for the discrimination tree. plus_invariance_of_isZTime takes [SuccOrder (coe D)] [IsSuccArchimedean (coe D)], so any application at D = intOrder must pass them positionally via inferInstanceAs, as ShiftSet.ofIntAction and WitnessFamily.std_isZTime already do.

The dispatch's lean-readiness block reported lean-lsp 'reachable', but the first lean_local_search of the dispatch returned index: unavailable with sources_searched: [source_text] only -- no language server running. Per the dispatch's own interpretation rule this is the degraded tier: every Mathlib and FormalSystem name in the report is evidenced by a grepped declaration site (file:line) rather than an LSP lookup, and no empty result was treated as proof of absence.

FrameOver.taskRel_eq_iter (FormalSystem/Semantics/IntNormalForm.lean:224) proves that EVERY regular frame over intOrder satisfies F.TaskRel w d u iff ofStepRel F.step w d u. The hgen-style generation hypothesis that saturation_of_orientedForest' takes as a parameter is therefore free for the base frame, so the headline cover theorem can be stated for an arbitrary [F.IsRegular] frame over intOrder with no generation side condition and no carrier identification.
